subject: Renewal request: Surge Protection add-on + term reset
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@orchidsys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal Q: Surge Protection add-on + term reset?

Marcus —

Quick note as we start the renewal conversation: we had two production interruptions in Q1 that triggered SLA reviews across the engineering execs. Orchard's legal and ops are pushing for stronger protections this renewal — specifically a Surge Protection add-on (guaranteed mitigation for spike-related latency), a term reset so we can align billing to our fiscal calendar, and a one-time invoice credit tied to recent incidents.

Budget is tight for FY29; we can commit to either a 24- or 36-month term if we get an upfront concession. Can you tell me what Redwood is willing to offer? Need a workable proposal by May 12 (contract expires May 15).

Thanks,
Carlos
Carlos Mendez
Head of Platform Ops, Orchid Systems
car los@orchidsys.com


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@orchidsys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 May 2028 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal Q: Surge Protection add-on + term reset?

Carlos —

Really appreciate the heads-up and the timeline. We want to keep Orchid on the platform — you’re a strategic account. I’m attaching a short comparison (Orchid_Renewal_Compare_v3.pdf) that shows a couple of paths:

- Path A: 24-month renewal + Surge Protection add-on, 15% first-year discount, one-time incident credit equal to 20% of April invoice.
- Path B: 36-month renewal + Surge Protection add-on, 12% Year 1 discount, $25k one-time credit, with a staggered pricing schedule.

I need to get a quick approval from Deal Desk / execs for any concession beyond the standard discount. I’ve looped in Vanessa and Priyom to help escalate. Can you confirm which term (24 v 36) Orchid would prefer if we can get approval for Path B? If you can sign by May 12 we’ll prioritize the SLA addendum and an expedited e-sign.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachment: Orchid_Renewal_Compare_v3.pdf

Marcus / Priyom —

Forwarding for Deal Desk visibility. Quick summary and recommended ask for execs:

1) Customer: Orchid Systems (strategic mid-market). Counter-offer request: Surge Protection SLA add-on, term reset to align with fiscal, and a one-time invoice credit tied to recent incidents.

2) Financial impact (est): Path A reduces TCV by ~18% YoY first year; Path B reduces near-term margin but improves 36mo NRR.

3) Recommendation for approval request: Approve Path B only if execs will allow $25k credit + 12% Year 1 discount and a contract term of 36 months with standard renewal escalation. Require legal to sign SLA addendum.

Attachments: Surge_Protection_SOW_stub.docx, proposed-term-sheet-ORCH.pdf

Marcus: please prepare a short executive note with deal_id DL-1789-ORCH and required approvals (discount %, one-time credit, term length, SLA addendum). I’ll flag with Finance if we need to push higher.

—Vanessa

- Surge Protection SLA add-on (new line item) — requires legal SLA addendum.
- Term: 36 months (customer prefers); current renewal would default to 12 months.

Subject: Re: Escalation: DL-1789-ORCH — approval request for renewal concessions

Thanks for the concise ask — I’ve reviewed the numbers. Approve the SLA add-on and the $25k one-time credit. Approve up to 15% discount for Year 1 on the condition that: 

- Legal signs the SLA addendum and we add standard incident-reporting timelines.
- The $25k credit is applied as an invoice credit (not cash payout).
- For any term longer than 24 months (i.e., 36 months), route to Lauren for final sign-off on extended commercial exposure — Lauren, can you greenlight 36mo? If not, Marcus, present Path B but note we may need a compensation plan for retention.

I want this to be a save, not an unlimited concession; cap discount at 15% and attach a quarterly quality review for the first year. With those conditions, Marcus — go ahead and send the revised DocuSign link and SLA addendum.

—Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations

- Year 1 discount: 15% (approved cap).
- One-time invoice credit: $25,000 applied to next invoice (approved, invoice-credit).
- Surge Protection add-on: included as a new line item; legal will push the SLA addendum to you for signature.

Attached: proposed-term-sheet-ORCH.pdf and Surge_Protection_SOW_stub.docx. DocuSign link (expiring 72 hours): https://www.docusign.com/sign/ORCH-DOC-5234

Please review and sign the SLA addendum + DocuSign by 2028-05-12 so we can process the credit and ensure continuous coverage. If Lauren requests final approval on the 36mo term, I’ll update you immediately.

Appreciate the partnership — we want Orchid to feel secure on the platform.
